# Sirach Chapter 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 31 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_031_page_001.jpg

---

31:1 Wakefulness over wealth wastes away the flesh, and the anxiety of it drives away sleep.

31:2 Wakeful anxiety cuts off slumber, and a grievous illness carries away sleep.

31:3 The rich man toils in gathering wealth, and when he rests he is filled with his delicacies.

31:4 The poor man toils in want of livelihood, and when he rests he becomes needy.

31:5 He who loves gold will not be justified, and he who pursues destruction will be filled with it.

31:6 Many have been given over to ruin on account of gold, and their destruction has met them face to face.

31:7 It is a stumbling block for those who sacrifice to it, and every fool will be taken captive by it.

31:8 Blessed is the rich man who is found blameless, and who has not gone after gold.

31:9 Who is he? And we will call him blessed, for he has done wonderful things among his people.

31:10 Who has been tested by it and found perfect? Then let it be a glory to him. Who was able to transgress and did not transgress, and to do evil and did not do it?

31:11 His good things will be made secure, and the assembly will recount his acts of charity.

31:12 Are you seated at the table of a great man? Do not open your gullet wide at it, and do not say, "What a great deal there is on it!"

31:13 Remember that an evil eye is a wicked thing. What has been created more evil than an eye? Therefore it sheds tears from every face.

31:14 Do not stretch out your hand wherever it looks, and do not crowd it in the dish with him.

31:15 Understand what your neighbor feels by your own experience, and be considerate in every matter.

31:16 Eat what is set before you like a well-bred person, and do not gnaw greedily, lest you be hated.

31:17 Be the first to stop for the sake of good manners, and do not be insatiable, lest you offend.

31:18 And if you are seated in the midst of many, do not stretch out your hand before them.

31:19 How sufficient is a little for a well-disciplined man! And he does not gasp upon his bed.

31:20 Healthy sleep comes from moderate eating; he rises early and his wits are with him. The pain of sleeplessness and colic and the torment of the belly are with the insatiable man.

31:21 And if you have been forced to eat, rise and go out and vomit, and you will have relief.

31:22 Hear me, my child, and do not despise me, and in the end you will find my words true. In all your works be quick, and no illness will come upon you.

31:23 Him who is generous with bread, men will speak well of him, and the testimony to his good character is trustworthy.

31:24 Him who is grudging with bread, the city will murmur against, and the testimony to his stinginess is accurate.

31:25 Do not show yourself valiant in wine, for wine has destroyed many.

31:26 The furnace proves the tempered blade; so wine proves hearts in the quarrel of the proud.

31:27 Wine is life for human beings if drunk in moderation. What is life to a man who is without wine? For it was created to make men glad.

31:28 Wine drunk at the proper time and in sufficient quantity is joy of heart and gladness of soul.

31:29 Wine drunk excessively is bitterness of soul, with provocation and stumbling.

31:30 Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool to his injury, reducing his strength and causing wounds.

31:31 Do not rebuke your neighbor at a wine feast, and do not despise him in his mirth. Speak no word of reproach to him, and do not distress him by making demands.
